turns.title: IgG4-related sialadenitis (Mikulicz disease) involving the submandibular glands

action.diagnosis: IgG4-related sialadenitis (Mikulicz disease) involving the submandibular glands
action.rationale: This 26-year-old woman presented with persistent, tender bilateral submandibular gland enlargement, odynophagia, dry mouth/eyes, and weight loss despite antibiotics. Imaging showed symmetrically enlarged submandibular glands with heterogeneous hypoechoic parenchyma and cystic spaces, without stones or masses. Serologies were notable for ANA positivity but negative anti-SSA/SSB, normal serum IgG4, and negative HIV/HCV. Minor labial salivary gland biopsy showed no focal lymphocytic sialadenitis (focus score 0) and no granulomas, making Sjögren syndrome and sarcoidosis unlikely. Submandibular gland biopsy showed a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with reactive lymphoid follicles, acinar atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and polytypic plasma cells, without lymphoepithelial lesions or obliterative phlebitis. Immunohistochemistry showed 19 IgG4-positive plasma cells per high-power field and an IgG4:IgG ratio greater than 0.5, meeting the histopathologic criteria for IgG4-related sialadenitis (Mikulicz disease), even though the serum IgG4 level was normal.

final.rationale: This 26-year-old woman presented with persistent, tender bilateral submandibular gland enlargement, odynophagia, dry mouth/eyes, and weight loss despite antibiotics. Imaging showed symmetrically enlarged submandibular glands with heterogeneous hypoechoic parenchyma and cystic spaces, without stones or masses. Serologies were notable for ANA positivity but negative anti-SSA/SSB, normal serum IgG4, and negative HIV/HCV. Minor labial salivary gland biopsy showed no focal lymphocytic sialadenitis (focus score 0) and no granulomas, making Sjögren syndrome and sarcoidosis unlikely. Submandibular gland biopsy showed a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with reactive lymphoid follicles, acinar atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and polytypic plasma cells, without lymphoepithelial lesions or obliterative phlebitis. Immunohistochemistry showed 19 IgG4-positive plasma cells per high-power field and an IgG4:IgG ratio greater than 0.5, meeting the histopathologic criteria for IgG4-related sialadenitis (Mikulicz disease), even though the serum IgG4 level was normal.

judgement.rationale: The candidate diagnosis is the same core disease as the reference—IgG4-related sialadenitis—and specifies the correct submandibular gland involvement; the added Mikulicz disease term is a related IgG4-related salivary gland disorder and does not change management.
